newsitem.title: USA: US economic activity key to policy--S.F. Fed Parry.
newsitem.headline: US economic activity key to policy--S.F. Fed Parry.

text.p: The key question for U.S. monetary policy today is whether or not the economy will slow down to more sustainable growth levels, said the head of the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco, Robert Parry.

Asked whether a strong jump in manufacturing activity in May as reported by the National Association of Purchasing Management could prompt the Fed to raise interest rates once again, Parry said that "The key is clearly whether this economy slows down or not to a sustainable rate of growth."

"We were growing at a 4.1 percent rate (between the first quarter of 1996 and the first quarter of 1997). I think that is a rate that is not sustainable. And after a while it would generate inflationary problems," Parry added.
Parry made his remarks during a question and answer session shortly after he delivered a speech on the Prospects for the Alaska and U.S. Economies here.
The National Association of Purchasing Management reported on Monday its manufacturing activity index jumped to 57.1 in May versus a 54.2 reading in April.

The Fed last raised rates on March 25, when it increased its target for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 5.50 percent. The central bank decided to leave rates unchanged during its last policy meeting on May 20.
